about: Held-out set for Milestone V (T109), written by a separate Claude subagent from FORMAT.md and spec 0010 only, without reading dev.json; all meetings, people and companies are synthetic (Trane is a fictional client). 30 meetings / 879 lines; 63 questions: 40 answerable (24 paraphrase, 14 person/date, 15 multipart/cross-meeting/follow-up), 12 unanswerable, 10 ambiguous/adversarial, 1 partial (incomplete index). Covers the four user scenarios (Andrew career goal last week, Trane staffing over the rolling last week, final 2027 planning decision incl. a no-decision variant, today's promised follow-ups with and without a 'Me' speaker), negation, changed plans, wrong-week and wrong-speaker distractors, two Andrews, names mentioned vs speakers vs attendees, DST/week boundary meetings (Sun 2026-10-25 22:00 -04:00, Sun 2026-11-01 23:30 -05:00, Mon 2026-11-02 00:30 -05:00), notes-only facts (required_notes = note indexes, extra key), an unindexed meeting, trim_before, delete_line, a corrected word, a deleted meeting, a planted prompt injection, prompt-exfiltration and scope-widening attempts, and follow-ups. Group rule used for counts: 'unanswerable' tag > 'ambiguous'/'adversarial' tag > partial > answerable.

meetings.title: Andrew / Simone 1:1
lines: Hey, can you hear me okay? My headphones were acting up earlier.
Yeah, loud and clear. How was the long weekend?
Good, quiet. We mostly stayed home. Okay, so what's on your list today?
A couple of things. First, the billing migration is mostly on track.
We moved the invoice tables over Tuesday, and the reconciliation job ran clean twice.
Nice. Any surprises?
Just the currency rounding thing, but Pilar already patched it.
Great. What else?
Um, so, the second thing is more about me.
One thing I want this half is the Kubernetes administrator certification. The company still pays for the exam, right?
It does, yeah. Learning budget covers the exam and one prep course.
Cool. I'd probably study evenings and sit it in December.
That sounds reasonable. Put it in your quarterly check-in doc so we can track it.
Will do.
Anything blocking you on the migration side?
Not really. The staging cluster is slow but that's a known thing.
Yeah, infra said they're adding nodes next week.
Okay, good.
How's the on-call load been?
Lighter. Two pages last rotation, both noise from the disk alert.
We should tune that alert. Can you open a ticket?
Sure, I'll file it after this.
Thanks. Oh, and the design review for the invoice export, is that still Thursday?
Thursday at two, yeah. Pilar's presenting.
Perfect. I might be a few minutes late, I have a conflict until two.
No worries, we'll start without you.
Anything else on your mind?
Oh, actually, one more. The reconciliation report needs a backup owner while Pilar's on vacation.
Let's sort that out next week.
Okay, I think that's it. Thanks.
Thanks, Andrew. Talk next week.

meetings.title: Andrew / Simone 1:1
lines: Hi, sorry, my previous meeting ran over.
No problem. I just grabbed coffee.
So, migration first? Or whatever you want.
Migration's basically done. We flipped the last of the customers on Monday.
That's huge. Congrats to the whole group.
Thanks. Pilar did most of the hard parts, honestly.
I'll make sure that's called out at the all hands.
Appreciate it. So, um, the bigger thing I wanted to talk about.
I've been thinking a lot about what's next for me.
Honestly, I think I'm ready to manage people, not just own systems.
When the payments group splits in January, I'd love to be considered for the lead spot.
Okay. That's great to hear, actually. What's drawing you to it?
I like the unblocking part. Running the migration, I liked coordinating more than coding, which surprised me.
That tracks with what I've seen.
Let's write that down as your growth plan for the next two quarters.
I'll talk to Beatrix about the split and what the lead role would look like.
Great. I'd still do the certification, but it's lower priority now.
Makes sense. Maybe start by running the weekly planning meeting for the group, as practice.
Yeah, I could do that starting next week.
Okay. Anything else?
The disk alert ticket got picked up, so we should see fewer pages.
Good. And how are you doing generally? It's been an intense month.
Tired, but fine. Looking forward to the holidays.
Fair. Take a Friday off sometime if you need it.
I might, thanks.
Alright, I'll follow up after I talk to Beatrix.
Sounds good.
Oh, and the hackathon judging notes, I'll send those over whenever.
Yeah, no rush.
Thanks, Andrew.

meetings.title: Team growth roundtable
lines: Okay, let's get started. This is the monthly growth roundtable, informal as always.
The idea is everyone shares one thing they want to work toward.
Can I go first? I've been sitting on this for a while.
Sure, go ahead, Joaquin.
So I'd like to try moving over to product management next year.
I've been doing a lot of the customer interviews already, and I like that side of it.
Love that. Have you talked to the product folks?
A little, with Wren. She said there might be an associate opening in the spring.
You'd be good at it. You already write better specs than half the PMs.
Ha, thanks. I'll take it.
Okay, who's next?
Um, me I guess. Mine is smaller. I want to get better at public speaking.
I'm going to submit a talk to the regional developer conference.
Great. What's the topic?
Probably the billing migration, how we did it with zero downtime.
Ooh. Andrew's been carrying that migration, you should loop him in.
Yeah, definitely. Honestly Andrew would be a natural lead, the way he ran it.
Agreed, but that's his call, not ours.
Andrew couldn't make it today, by the way, he's at the dentist.
Lucky him.
Ha.
Okay, and for me, I want to delegate more. I'm in too many meetings.
That's an easy one to say and a hard one to do.
Tell me about it.
Are we doing the mentoring pairs again this year?
Yes, the sign up sheet goes out next week.
Can we pair across teams this time? Last year was all within the team.
Good idea, I'll suggest it.
Also, the learning budget, does it reset in January?
It does, so use it or lose it for this year.
Noted. I've got a course I've been eyeing.
Okay, I think that's everyone. Thanks all.

meetings.title: Andrew / Simone 1:1
lines: Hey, happy November. Did the time change mess you up?
A little. My kid was up at five thinking it was six.
Classic. Okay, what do you have?
So, first, I ran the planning meeting for the payments group on Monday. It went fine.
Nice, how did it feel?
Honestly, it was useful. And it also made me rethink something.
About the lead thing we talked about last week.
I've been thinking, and I'd rather stay hands-on through next year.
I talked it over at home too. With the new baby coming in the spring, I don't want to take on a team right now.
That's completely fair. Thanks for telling me early.
Maybe we revisit it next fall? I don't want to close the door.
Sure. I'll let Beatrix know to hold off on considering you for the January split.
Thanks. I'd still like to keep running the weekly planning, if that's okay.
Absolutely, that's good practice either way.
And the certification, back on the table then?
Yeah, I'll sit the exam in December like I originally planned.
Great. Other stuff?
The invoice export shipped. A few support tickets, nothing big.
Good. Any feedback from finance?
They want a CSV option. I told them maybe next quarter.
Fine. Let's not promise dates.
Agreed.
Oh, the on-call swap for Thanksgiving week, did you find someone?
Pilar took it, I'm taking her Christmas shift.
Perfect.
That's it from me.
Okay. Congrats on the baby news, by the way.
Thanks! We're excited.
Talk next week.
Bye.

meetings.title: Trane kickoff prep
lines: Okay, the Trane kickoff is in two weeks. Let's figure out what we're missing.
The SOW is signed, the kickoff deck is half done.
Who's presenting the integration plan?
I can, unless the client wants their own architect to lead it.
They mentioned their architect is out until mid November.
Okay, so we present. Fine.
Bigger question is people. Who do we put on Trane?
For Trane we could ask Theo, he's pretty light right now.
Theo's light this week, but I think he's getting pulled onto the Halvorsen bid.
Let's not commit anyone yet. I want to see the December forecast first.
Fair.
We also need someone who knows building controls. That's the tricky part.
Right, the BACnet stuff. Very few of us have done it.
Kofi has. He did the hospital project.
Kofi's buried in Northgate though.
Yeah, Northgate's not letting go of him soon.
Okay, park it. Let's revisit next week.
On the deck, do we want the timeline slide or keep it vague?
Timeline, but with ranges, not dates.
And the risks slide?
Keep it short. Three risks, max.
Data access, controls integration, and their change freeze in December.
Good.
Who's sending the agenda to the client?
I will, today.
Thanks. Anything else on Trane?
Travel. Are we going on site for the kickoff?
Probably, Columbus, one day. I'll check the budget.
Okay.
Alright, thanks everyone.

meetings.title: Trane weekly
lines: Morning. Let's start, we've got a lot.
Morning. Did everyone survive the clock change?
Barely.
Okay. Status on the Trane data access request?
Their IT approved read access to the historian. VPN credentials should come Wednesday.
Good. And the kickoff deck is final?
Final as of Friday. I sent the PDF.
Great. So the open question is still bandwidth for Trane's controls integration.
Honestly, Kofi could probably pick some of it up once the Northgate cutover is done.
That's supposed to be mid November, but I wouldn't bet on it.
Okay, so maybe Kofi, not before the sixteenth.
What about Priyanka? She knows the analytics side.
Priyanka told me she's at about sixty percent through December, so she has some room.
Sixty percent busy or sixty percent free?
Busy. So roughly two days a week free.
Okay, that's useful for the analytics piece, not the controls work.
Agreed, controls needs someone close to full time.
Let's take this to the resourcing sync on Wednesday.
Sounds good.
Next, the client's change freeze.
They confirmed it starts December eighteenth.
So anything on their side needs to land before that.
We should front load the historian connector then.
Yes. Can you sketch a plan for that?
Sure, I'll draft one by Thursday.
Should we schedule a weekly with their architect once he's back?
Yes, starting the week of the sixteenth.
I'll set it up.
Anything else?
Just that their procurement wants our insurance certificate again.
I'll resend it.
Okay, thanks all.

meetings.title: Resourcing sync
lines: Okay, resourcing sync. Three things: support coverage, Trane, and the December forecast.
Let's do support first, it's on fire.
Go.
So response times went from about four hours to almost two days last week.
Mostly because Wyatt and Corinne were both out sick at the same time.
And the new ticket form doubled volume, people are filing everything.
Okay. What's the fix?
Short term, we're adding a weekend rotation starting the fourteenth.
Two people each Saturday, rotating, and we'll pay the on-call stipend.
Fine by me. And the form?
We'll put the required category field back, that should cut the junk.
Good. Next, Trane.
We still need someone on the controls integration.
So, good news there. Lucia's freed up now that Halvorsen got pushed to Q1.
Oh, really? When did that happen?
Yesterday. The client delayed their board approval.
Lucia did the BACnet work on the airport job, right?
Yes, she's probably our best person for it.
Okay, let's put Lucia on Trane starting Monday. I'll tell her today.
What about Kofi? We'd floated him on Monday.
Northgate slipped again, so Kofi's out until at least December.
Okay, so not Kofi. Lucia for controls, Priyanka part time for analytics.
Do we need to confirm Priyanka with her manager?
Yeah, I'll ask. Let's treat her as tentative until then.
Off the record, Theo is going on leave in December, so don't plan around him.
Okay. Last thing, the December forecast.
We're at about eighty five percent billable, which is fine.
Halvorsen slipping hurts January though.
Let's look at that in two weeks.
Works for me.
Thanks, everyone.

meetings.title: Trane client check-in
lines: Hi Dale, thanks for making time.
Of course. Happy to be here.
Quick update on our side. We've finalized staffing for the controls work.
Lucia accepted yesterday, so she's officially on Trane starting the ninth.
Hi, I'm Lucia. I'll be your main contact for the controls integration.
Great to meet you. Have you worked with a building automation system like ours before?
Similar ones. I did a BACnet integration for an airport last year.
Perfect. Our architect gets back the sixteenth, he'll want to meet you.
Happy to. I'll send some times.
And on analytics, we'll have part time support, details next week.
Okay. What do you need from us right now?
Mostly the point list export from your controls server, and access to the historian.
The historian access should be done Wednesday, I saw the ticket.
Great, that matches what we heard.
And remind me about the change freeze?
Yours starts December eighteenth, so we're front loading the connector work.
Good. Our facilities team will be relieved.
Is there a test building we can use?
Yes, the Dayton warehouse. Low risk, smaller system.
That's ideal.
Okay, we'll send a revised timeline Monday.
Sounds good. Anything else from us?
Just the insurance certificate, we resent it Tuesday.
Got it, procurement confirmed.
Looking forward to working together.
Likewise. Talk soon.
Thanks Dale, bye.
Bye.
Okay, that went well.
Yeah, he seems easy to work with.

meetings.title: 2027 planning kickoff
lines: Okay, this is the first pass at the 2027 plan. Nothing here is final.
I want us to leave with a short list of candidate bets.
I'll start. I think mid-market is the obvious one. Our pipeline there doubled.
Mid-market, sure, but we'd need a sales team that doesn't exist yet.
That's part of the plan, hire it.
My candidate is retiring the legacy billing system. It's eating a whole team.
Is that a bet or just hygiene?
It's hygiene with a big payoff. About twenty percent of our infra cost.
And mine is opening a Lisbon engineering hub. Hiring here is brutal.
Okay, so three: mid-market, billing retirement, Lisbon.
Someone also floated moving the Denver office downtown, but that's facilities, not strategy.
Let's leave that off this list.
What about pricing? We haven't touched it in two years.
Pricing changes for 2027 should be their own working group. Noor, can you run that?
Sure. I'll set something up for late October.
Great.
What's the timeline for locking the plan?
I'd like a decision at the offsite on the twenty third.
That's tight.
It is, but the board meets in November.
Okay, I'll write up the mid-market case.
I'll do Lisbon.
Billing, me.
Two pages each, max. Send by the twentieth.
Two pages, got it.
Can we include cost estimates or keep it narrative?
Rough costs, ranges are fine.
Okay.
Alright, good start. Thanks everyone.
Thanks.

meetings.title: Leadership offsite
lines: Okay, welcome everyone. Agenda is the 2027 plan, then a quick security update.
You've all read the three write-ups. Let's go bet by bet.
Mid-market. The case is pipeline growth, and the numbers held up.
The cost is hiring eight sellers. That's real money.
It pays back in about eighteen months on the conservative case.
Questions on mid-market? No? Okay.
Lisbon. Honestly, after writing it up, I think it's premature.
We'd be opening a hub while also building a sales team. Too much at once.
I agree. Defer it a year.
And billing retirement?
Everyone agrees on that one, I think. It's funded either way.
Okay, so we're agreed: the 2027 plan is mid-market first, billing retirement funded, Lisbon hiring deferred.
Let's call that final, and I'll take it to the board.
Final, yes.
Yes.
Great. Imogen, security update?
Sure. Quick one. The pen test came back last week.
The big finding was the admin panel exposed on staging. No customer data, but bad.
We'll have it locked behind the VPN by Tuesday.
Anything else critical?
Two other criticals, both in the old billing service, which is another reason to retire it.
Ha, convenient.
Also the SOC 2 fieldwork starts in November, so expect evidence requests.
Okay. Can you send a list of what each team needs to prepare?
Yes, by the end of next week.
Thanks. Anything else before lunch?
Just to confirm, are we telling the wider company about the plan?
Not until after the board. Keep it in this room.
Understood.
Okay, lunch. Thanks all.

notes.text: 2027 plan: mid-market first, billing retirement funded, Lisbon hub deferred. Rhea takes it to the board.

meetings.title: Pricing working group
lines: Okay, pricing working group, session one. The goal today is options, not decisions.
I have two proposals for 2027.
Option one, move from per seat to usage based for the analytics add-on.
Option two, keep per seat but add a cheaper starter tier.
The starter tier worries me. It could cannibalize the mid tier.
Do we have data on that?
Some. About a third of mid tier accounts use less than half their seats.
Which is an argument for usage based, honestly.
Or an argument that they'd downgrade.
Okay, let's not settle it today. I want finance to model both.
How long does finance need?
Odile said three weeks.
So mid November at the earliest.
Right. And then it goes to exec staff.
Should we talk to customers first?
Yes, five or six interviews. Can you set those up?
I'll ask the account managers for names.
Separately, marketing asked whether a price change affects their Q4 campaigns.
It doesn't, nothing changes this year.
Good, because they said their Q4 spend will probably land around two hundred k and it's mostly committed.
That's their number, not ours. Fine.
Do we grandfather existing customers if we change pricing?
Probably for a year, but again, not deciding today.
Okay.
Next session in two weeks. Bring the interview notes.
Will do.
Should we invite sales?
Yes, invite Bram's team lead.
Okay.
Thanks everyone.

meetings.title: Exec staff
lines: Morning. A few items. First, I need to reopen the 2027 plan.
Uh oh.
I previewed it with two board members on Friday.
They pushed back hard on mid-market. They think the sales hiring is too risky in this market.
They want us to look at the partner channel instead, resellers.
So the offsite decision is off?
Not off, but it's not final anymore. Nothing is locked until the board review on the nineteenth.
Do we need new write-ups?
Yes, a partner channel case. Two pages, same format.
I can do that, I ran partners at my last company.
Great. By the twelfth, please.
Does billing retirement stay?
Yes, that one nobody questioned.
And Lisbon is still deferred?
Still deferred.
Okay. That's a big swing, though. I'd hate to lose a year debating.
Agreed, which is why the nineteenth is a hard date.
Second item?
Yes, the holiday schedule. The office closes the twenty fourth through the first.
Same as last year.
Same as last year. Third, the all hands next week.
Are we presenting the plan there?
No, not until after the board review.
Got it.
Are we doing the holiday party in person this year?
Yes, December twelfth, details from the office team.
Okay.
Last item, Atlas. Product will cover it on Wednesday.
Okay.
That's it, thanks.

meetings.title: Platform standup
lines: Morning. Let's go quick, it's Friday.
Morning.
Hey.
Okay, me first. I finished the migration checklist review yesterday.
I'll send the revised migration checklist to the group by end of day.
Thanks. I'm still stuck on the flaky checkout test.
I can look at it properly, but only if Rohan's PR lands first. It touches the same fixture.
Did Rohan say when?
He said maybe this afternoon.
Okay. Marta, can you take the vendor follow-up on the certificate renewal?
Sure, I'll email them by Tuesday.
Great, thanks.
For me, the queue consumer upgrade is done in staging.
I want to roll it to production Monday morning, if nobody objects.
Monday's fine. Not Friday, please.
Ha, no, definitely not Friday.
Maybe someone should update the on-call runbook at some point, it still mentions the old queue.
Yeah, good point. Let's put it on the board.
Also the staging database is almost out of disk again.
Ugh. I'll ping infra about it after standup.
They said they were adding storage this week.
I'll check whether that actually happened.
Is the Thursday demo still on?
Yes, I'll book the room.
Can we do it remote? Half of us are home on Thursdays.
Fine, I'll set up a call instead of a room.
Oh, and I'm out Wednesday afternoon, dentist.
Okay, that's all from me.
Same.
Alright, have a good weekend.

meetings.title: Brightwater onboarding call
lines: Hi, thanks for joining. Tessa's here too, from our ops team.
Hi everyone.
Hi, thanks both. So the goal today is to close out the open onboarding items.
Great. The big one for us is pricing for the extra sites.
Right. I'll get you the revised quote by Monday noon.
Perfect. And the security questionnaire?
I'll loop in our security lead, assuming legal signs off on the NDA first.
We sent the NDA back yesterday, so that should be quick.
Great, then it should happen early next week.
What about the sandbox environment?
Jonah on our side will set up the sandbox, he's the one who owns that.
Okay. Timeline?
I'd guess end of next week, but that's Jonah's call. I'll confirm the date with him.
And from our side, we'll send the data sample by Wednesday.
That'd be great.
One question. Should we do a pilot at one site first?
It might be worth doing a pilot, yeah. Let's discuss once you've seen the quote.
Sounds good.
Training for our staff, how does that work?
We usually do two remote sessions, scheduled once the sandbox is up.
Okay.
And billing, who should we send invoice questions to?
Our finance team. I'll send you their shared address right after this call.
Thanks.
Anything else on your list?
I think that's everything.
Same. Thanks, this was helpful.
Thanks both, talk soon.
Bye.
Bye.

meetings.title: Team retro
lines: Okay, retro time. What went well this cycle?
The release went out on time, first time in a while.
And the new review checklist helped, fewer bounced PRs.
Agreed. What didn't go well?
Too many interruptions. Support pings in the team channel all day.
And the staging environment was flaky, again.
Okay. For interruptions, let's try a support shield person each week.
I like that. Rotating?
Rotating, yeah. I'll write up the retro notes and the shield rotation and share them by Monday.
Can we also get infra to look at staging?
I'll raise it with infra in Tuesday's sync.
Thanks.
One more, the release notes were late.
That's on me, I'll start drafting them earlier next time.
Cool. Anything else?
Shout out to Pilar for the export fix.
Yes, agreed.
Should we keep the retro at forty five minutes? Today felt rushed.
Let's try an hour next time.
Can we do it Wednesdays instead of Thursdays? Thursdays are packed.
Possibly, I'll check the calendar.
Also the planning poker thing, are we keeping it?
I'd drop it, honestly. It takes forever.
Let's drop it for a cycle and see.
Fine with me.
Also snacks. We need better snacks.
Ha. Seconded.
I'll pass that along to office ops.
Thank you.
Okay, good retro. Thanks all.

meetings.title: Atlas launch planning
lines: Okay, Atlas. Where are we?
Feature complete as of Friday. QA is running the full regression this week.
And the date?
We're planning to ship Atlas on November seventeenth.
App store review usually takes two or three days, so we submit by the twelfth.
Is marketing aligned on the seventeenth?
Yes, the launch email and blog post are drafted.
Good. Any risks?
The new consent screen still needs legal sign off.
When is legal looking at it?
They said end of the month.
That's cutting it close.
It's a small screen, it should be fine.
Famous last words. Let's flag it.
Beta feedback is mostly positive. The crash rate is under half a percent.
What are the top complaints?
Onboarding is too long, and the dark mode colors on Android.
We fixed dark mode in the last build.
And onboarding?
We cut two screens. Testing it now.
Okay. How big is the beta right now?
About eight thousand testers.
We'll expand it before launch.
Support readiness?
Help center articles are in review. Support training is on the ninth.
Good. Press?
Two outlets have embargoed copies lined up.
Okay. Let's meet again next Thursday for go no-go prep.
Sounds good.
Thanks.

meetings.title: Atlas go/no-go prep
lines: Okay, go no-go prep. Let's start with the elephant in the room.
The date.
Yes. Some people think we should move the launch to December, to be safe.
I was one of them, to be fair.
I know. But to be clear, we are not moving the launch. The seventeenth stands.
Okay. What changed your mind?
Legal looked at the consent screen early and only had minor wording edits.
Fair enough. If legal's fine, I'm fine.
So we still submit to the store on the twelfth?
Yes, the twelfth.
Then marketing keeps the email for the seventeenth.
Correct. Next, the beta expansion.
We'd like to open it wider. More devices, more crash data.
How wide?
I'll have a number by next week, depends on the server budget.
Okay. Launch day on-call?
Two engineers plus me. We'll have a war room channel.
Good. And support?
Training happened, they felt ready. A few questions about refunds.
Send those to finance.
Will do.
Should we do a soft launch in Canada first?
No, it adds complexity. Same day everywhere.
Okay.
Press embargo lifts at nine eastern on launch day.
Make sure the blog post goes live at the same time.
I'll coordinate with marketing.
Anything else that could stop us?
Not that I know of.
Good. Final go no-go is the twelfth, right before submission.
Got it.
Thanks all.

meetings.title: Atlas launch update
lines: Okay, change of plan, and I want to explain it carefully.
Legal did the final review of the consent screen on Monday.
They found the data sharing toggle defaults to on, which doesn't work for the EU.
Oh no.
So the launch moves to December first. Store submission on the twenty fourth.
Is that firm?
Firm. Legal needs a week with the new flow, and then we need a fresh build.
We can have the toggle fix in by Friday. It's small.
Good, but legal still needs their week.
Marketing will need to move the email and the press embargo.
I'll call both outlets today.
Thanks.
For the beta, we'll cap it at fifteen thousand testers, opening Friday.
Is the server budget okay with that?
Yes, finance approved it yesterday.
Great. That gives us a lot more crash data before December.
Do we tell beta testers about the new date?
Yes, in the release notes, keep it simple.
Should we use the extra time for the onboarding changes?
Only the ones already tested. No new features.
Agreed, no scope creep.
The Android dark mode fix also gets more soak time, which is nice.
Silver lining.
What about the Thanksgiving week? Half the team is out.
That's why submission is the twenty fourth, before the holiday.
Makes sense.
Anything else?
No, I'll update the launch doc.
Thanks everyone.
Thanks.

meetings.title: Weekend deploy check
lines: Hey, thanks for jumping on, I know it's Sunday night.
No worries. How's the deploy looking?
The new cache layer went out at eight. Hit rate is climbing, about sixty percent so far.
Latency?
Down about thirty milliseconds at p95. Pretty good.
Any errors?
A handful of timeouts on the session service, but they look like warm up.
Okay. What's the plan if it gets worse overnight?
If the cache change misbehaves overnight, we roll back the cache change first thing Monday.
Who's watching it overnight?
The on-call in Singapore. I left them a note.
Good. The database looks fine?
Yeah, the primary is quiet. Nothing weird.
Okay.
I'll check again at seven before standup.
Should we post in the incident channel?
Not an incident. Just a note in the deploy channel.
Fair.
By the way, are you around next weekend? The clocks change.
I am, but I'm not thrilled about it.
Ha. The scheduler had a bug last year with the repeated hour.
I remember. We patched it, right?
We did, but let's keep an eye on it.
Okay.
Alright, that's it. Thanks.
Night.
Night.
Oh wait, did the status pages move to the new host?
Not yet, Tuesday.
Okay, night.

meetings.title: Late incident bridge
lines: Okay, I'm on. What do we know?
The primary database in Virginia started throwing storage latency alerts at eleven.
Write latency is over two seconds. Checkout is timing out for some users.
Is it the volume or the instance?
The provider status page says degraded storage in that zone.
Okay. My recommendation is we fail over to the Ohio replica now, and fail back after the storage patch.
How far behind is the replica?
Under a second of lag.
Then the data loss risk is basically nothing. Let's do it.
Do we need approval from anyone?
I'm incident commander, it's my call. Failing over.
Starting the failover.
I'll post in the status page.
Thanks. Keep the message short, degraded checkout, mitigation in progress.
Failover complete. Writes are going to Ohio.
Checkout errors are dropping.
Good. Let's watch it for ten minutes.
The alert timestamps look odd, by the way, because of the time change this morning.
Yeah, ignore the duplicate hour in the logs.
Error rate is back to baseline.
Great. I'll write up a summary tonight.
Do we fail back in the morning?
No, not until the provider confirms the storage patch.
Okay.
Let's do a follow-up in an hour to confirm stability.
Works.
Status page updated to monitoring.
Thanks both. Talk in an hour.
Bye.
Bye.

meetings.title: Incident follow-up
lines: Okay, follow-up. Is it still stable?
Stable. Error rate flat for the last hour.
Good. The provider says the storage patch rolls out over the next two days.
So we'll keep running on the Ohio replica through Wednesday, then fail back during the maintenance window.
Should we also roll back the cache change from last week, just in case?
No, the cache change is unrelated, leave it.
Okay.
While you're all here, a quick security note since I'm on anyway.
The pen test follow-up: all the criticals are closed now, and two mediums remain.
The auditors come back on the twentieth for the SOC 2 fieldwork.
Good to hear. Do you need anything from my team?
Just the change logs for the failover, for the evidence folder.
I'll export those tomorrow.
Thanks.
Okay, postmortem. I'll own it, draft by Thursday.
Do we need a customer email?
Support says only about two hundred users hit errors. A status page note is enough.
Okay.
Any chance this was related to the clock change?
No, it was the provider. Timing was just bad luck.
Ha, of course.
Okay, let's get some sleep.
Good night.
Night.
One last thing, set the alert threshold back to normal before you log off.
Already done.
Perfect.
Bye.
Bye.
Bye.

meetings.title: Staff designer debrief
lines: Okay, debrief for the staff designer loop. Let's go around.
I'm a strong yes on Sabine. Her systems thinking was the best we've seen.
Yes from me too. The portfolio review was excellent.
Any concerns?
Maybe a little light on design systems governance, but that's learnable.
Agreed, it's minor.
Okay. I'm a yes as well. So we recommend making an offer.
Do we know her salary expectations?
Recruiting has them, I haven't seen the number.
Honestly, I think the panel was too big. Five interviewers for one role is a lot.
Yeah, she mentioned it felt like a marathon.
Fair. Owen told me he'd rather not be on the panel again, he's stretched thin with the rebrand.
Makes sense. We can drop to four next time.
Let's do four, and rotate who sits in.
Who's checking references?
I'll do two, recruiting does the third.
Should we tell the other finalist now or wait?
Wait until the offer is accepted.
Okay.
Recruiting will handle the timing once the offer is out.
Will she report to you or to the design lead?
To the design lead, dotted line to me.
What team does she start on?
Checkout redesign first, then the design system.
Good, that plays to her strengths.
Can we send her the onboarding packet early?
After she signs, yes.
Okay, I think we're done.
Thanks, great loop everyone.
Thanks.

Wow. Okay.
Alright, Q3 retrospective. Let's start with wins.
We hit the uptime target every month.
And the onboarding time for new engineers went from three weeks to under two.
Great. What hurt?
Hiring was slow. Two roles open for the whole quarter.
And we underestimated the billing migration by a month.
Fair. What would we change?
Estimate migrations with a buffer, like fifty percent.

Okay, noted. Next, the team dinner.
Are we doing the Portuguese place again?
Yes, I was thinking Thursday the twelfth.
They're closed Thursdays, I checked last time.

Wednesday works for me.
Same.
Okay, Wednesday the eleventh, seven o'clock. I'll make the reservation.
Can partners come?
Not this time, it's team only.
Okay.

Alright, thanks everyone.
Thanks.
Bye.

Later.

Finally.
